# Card

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For content that belongs together on a page: a summary, a report, a plan to choose. Its
radius is the box step, never a control's, so a card never reads as a button. It is not
interactive itself; what the user can do goes in the footer as a Button.

```tsx
<CardRoot>
  <CardHeader><h2>Monthly report</h2></CardHeader>
  <CardBody>Revenue rose 12% against April, driven by renewals.</CardBody>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Download PDF</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</CardRoot>
```

Every part is a flat export: `CardRoot`, `CardHeader`, `CardBody`, `CardFooter` and
`CardSkeleton`; there is no `Card`. `CardHeader` sets the type of the title and leaves the
heading level to you. `CardBody` is a block, so space several paragraphs yourself.
`CardSkeleton` holds the full width at 5:2 while data loads; pass the real height in
`className`.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import {
  CardRoot,
  CardHeader,
  CardBody,
  CardFooter,
  CardSkeleton,
} from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

### CardRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The parts, in order: CardHeader, CardBody and CardFooter. Each one is optional. |

### CardHeader

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The title, in the heading element the page outline needs. |

### CardBody

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The text. Several paragraphs are spaced by the caller. |

### CardFooter

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The actions, in a row that wraps when the card is narrow. |

### CardSkeleton

This part takes no design props of its own.

Anything else is passed to the element each part draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
